v1 structural 1/3: scan-first FIFO drain + CLOCK(2-bit freq) general list, promote scan pages touched by GET threads, index-page protection

baseline 2: reference/s3fifo.c unchanged. Context: get_scan.c scored 502 (2.4x below noop ~1215) on pc306; hypothesis H1 = get_scan proposes no victims when scan_pids empty. s3fifo needs no scan_pids.
calibration: unmodified noop.c (kernel default reclaim) on my host, to check whether ~500 ops/s BPF policies are below the ~1215 noop reference
structural 1/3 scan-aware S3-FIFO: scan-pid list evicted first (256-page reserve, GET-touched scan pages promoted), small FIFO 10% + CLOCK main freq<=3 + ghost; only non-scan accesses count
scan-aware S3-FIFO: scan-pid folios -> scan list evicted first (promote to main if GET-touched); GET folios -> small FIFO(10%)/CLOCK main; scan-thread accesses don't raise freq

structural 1/3 scan-aware S3-FIFO (compile fix): scan-pid list evicted first (256-page reserve, GET-touched scan pages promoted), small FIFO 10% + CLOCK main freq<=3 + ghost; only non-scan accesses count

s3fifo + LevelDB index-block pinning: last page of each file admitted straight to main w/ freq 3 and skipped by main CLOCK. Base: my s3fifo baseline 642 (noop=561 per jack-sparrow). Lane distinct from scan-aware s3fifo (ahab/davy).
structural 1/3 scan-aware S3-FIFO (compile fix 2: static size counters): scan-pid list evicted first (256-page reserve), small FIFO 10% + CLOCK main + ghost

scan-aware S3-FIFO (fixed ctx compile err): scan-pid folios -> scan list evicted first (promote to main if GET-touched); GET folios -> small FIFO(10%)/CLOCK main freq<=3; scan-thread accesses ignored; no ghost

v2: scan-only minimal-overhead policy (no per-folio map, no folio_accessed); evict scan-pid pages FIFO first, propose nothing else -> kernel default for GET pages. Tests CPU-overhead hypothesis (noop 561 > v1 518 > get_scan 498)
baseline 3: reference/sampling.c unchanged (sampled LFU k=20 + index bonus). Question: does pure frequency beat s3fifo (642) on Zipfian GETs? index pinning on s3fifo was neutral (635).

falsification A/B on s3fifo ref (642): scan-pid-inserted folios admitted straight to main (opposite of scan-first eviction). Tests hypothesis that scan pages are reused and scan-protection, not scan-eviction, raises throughput (rbytes correlates + with tput across all attempts)
scan-aware S3-FIFO v2 (2/3): ghost ALL non-scan evictions (incl MAIN), ghost 64k entries storing freq; ghost hit -> MAIN with freq=min(2,1+ghostfreq)

s3fifo knob 1/3: small queue 25% of cache (ref: cache/15 or main<=2*small). Hypothesis: 800-page small window too short for warm Zipfian GET pages to earn promotion. Observation: rios ~constant 11.1-11.6k across all policies -> IOPS-bound; score tracks ops/IO (s3fifo 1.66, sampling 1.44, get_scan 1.35).

v3: v2 scan-only with SCAN_MIN_PAGES 32->2048 (8MiB reserve). Tests readahead-thrash hypothesis: rios ~constant across all policies, score tracks KB/rio; small-reserve scan-first eviction shrinks KB/rio

diagnostic: reference/fifo.c unchanged (no accessed hook, no maps). Bytes/op is ~9.1-9.6KB across ALL attempts (miss rate ~policy-invariant) -> testing whether throughput is set by eviction-path cost rather than hit ratio. If FIFO ~= s3fifo 640, policy quality is not the lever
ablation 3/3: v2 with scan-pid special casing OFF (no scan list, scan accesses count) -> plain S3-FIFO + ghost-all w/ freq. Tests hypothesis that zipfian scan start keys give scan pages real reuse
lane change (scan-first lane closed: reserve 32->2048 gave 523->528, all scan-first policies < noop 561 < s3fifo 641; scan pages appear reusable). Untested-base probe: reference/mglru.c unchanged

structural 1/3 readahead-aware s3fifo: eager promotion to main in folio_accessed (list_move) + never-accessed small folios (freq 0, e.g. unconsumed readahead) get one extra lap in small FIFO; main fallback if small yields too few. Hypothesis: IOPS-bound + bytes/op ~constant => score tracks bytes/IO; s3fifo 15.5KB/IO vs get_scan 12.5KB/IO; protect readahead from thrash.

reference/mglru.c unchanged (untested reference). Context: fifo 628 ~= s3fifo 642 > noop 561 -> hit-ratio quality weakly matters; rios ~10-12k for all policies (disk-bound ~300 IOPS?), score ~ ops per disk I/O

hypothesis test: LevelDB block cache sits above page cache, so page-cache hit signal is inverted (2nd-level cache). Evidence: LFU 498-540 < LRU noop 561/mglru 565 < FIFO 628 ~ S3-FIFO 641. Test: reference/mru.c unchanged; if MRU >= FIFO, exclusive-caching view confirmed

structural 2/3 access-aware s3fifo: INVERT eval#5's lap rule. Eval#5 (lap for freq-0) = 615, bytes/IO unchanged (15.5KB) -> readahead-thrash hypothesis refuted; bytes/op rose -> unused readahead neighbours of GET misses pollute small. Now: freq0 evicted at once, freq1 gets one extra small lap; eager promotion kept.

structural 1/3 NEW-filtered S3-FIFO: never-accessed folios (GET readahead junk) in NEW list evicted first beyond 512-page reserve; first access -> SMALL; PG_referenced at add -> SMALL; else as f4670f97 (642)

falsification (mirror of my scan-first v3=528): GET-FIRST two-FIFO - GET pages evicted first beyond 2048-page reserve, scan-pid pages protected. Family map so far: LFU 498-540 < MRU 527 < LRU noop 561/mglru 565 < FIFO 628 ~ S3-FIFO 641; scan-first always < baseline. Tests whether scan pages are the valuable class

structural 3/3 ablation: reference s3fifo + ONLY eager promotion (list_move to main in folio_accessed on 2nd hit). Evals #5/#6 (both w/ eager promotion + opposite lap rules) = 615/610 vs ref 642 -> isolates whether hook-time list_move is the cost.

structural 1/3 history-LFU: single list, sampled (16) eviction of min frequency; freq in 2^20-slot array keyed hash(ino,index) that SURVIVES eviction (sampling ref 541 forgets counts on evict); no per-folio map; lazy halving per 2^18 accesses
long-memory ghost: f4670f97 (642) with ghost 64k per-CPU-LRU -> 256k common LRU (~20x cache). Two-level-cache view: page-cache reuse distances are long, ghost hits = warm signal

structural 1/3 history-LFU (retry; prev fail = 'struct slot' clashes with vmlinux.h, renamed): single list, sampled(16) min-freq eviction, freq in 2^20 array keyed hash(ino,index) surviving eviction, no per-folio map

s3fifo ghost 4x cache (ref 1x). Rationale: LevelDB block cache above page cache makes page-cache reuse distances long (exclusive-cache view, cf jack-sparrow 30244447); bigger ghost admits more medium-reuse GET pages to main. Closed my lane: eager promotion alone 628 (vs ~638 ref avg), lap rules 610/615.

HOST CALIBRATION WARNING: pc320 (mine) is ~12% slower than pc319: mglru.c = 565 here vs 645 on davy's pc319; my noop 561 => kernel default ~= fifo ~= s3fifo ~= mglru (all ~640 on fast hosts). My earlier 'family ranking' (LRU < FIFO) was a host artifact; only within-host comparisons are valid. On pc320: noop 561, mglru 565, MRU 527, scan-first 518-528, GET-first 528. Now: last untested reference, lhd.c unchanged

s3fifo + consumed-scan-first: scan-inserted folios move to a consumed list on the scan's first READ and that list is evicted first (GET-touched -> main); unread readahead stays in s3fifo queues. Tests readahead-thrash explanation of why scan-first eviction lost (608 vs 642)

reviewer: reference/mglru.c unchanged on pc306 to resolve 645 (davy) vs 565 (jack) cross-host split for identical code. My s3fifo-family baseline on pc306: 642/635/633/637 (4 near-identical variants, noise ~+-5).

REVIEW/falsification: does s3fifo actually beat kernel default? Only I have measured noop (561 on pc320); team compares s3fifo 641 (pc306) to noop across hosts, but pc320 is ~12% slow (mglru 565 here vs 645 pc319). reference/s3fifo.c unchanged on pc320: ~561 => policies are flat vs kernel default; ~630+ => real gain. LHD here = 453 (sampling-based policies all lose, low KB/rio)

structural 2/3 history-LFU: v1 (544, 925ce075) + count at most one access per page per 2ms (scan thread reads many keys/page in a burst -> v1 likely pinned scan pages with huge counts); sketch 2^19 slots
calibration on fast host pc309: unmodified noop.c (kernel default, comment-only change). Open question: is kernel default ~640 on fast hosts (pc320 noop=561)?

structural 1/3 mglru+ghost-admission: reference mglru (652 on pc306, my best) but refaulting folios (ghost hit, 400k-entry ghost) are added to youngest gen max_seq instead of oldest/2nd-oldest. Ref mglru uses ghost only for tier refault stats; s3fifo's edge over FIFO is ghost admission.

mglru-tune 1/3 (engineer lane: MGLRU is best within-host on pc306 651.8 vs s3fifo 641.8 and on pc320 565 vs s3fifo 544). Ablation: insert new folios at gen-list TAIL instead of head (ref list_add + head-first eviction = newest-inserted evicted first within oldest gen). Compare to my mglru ref 565

structural 1/3 (retry, verifier fix) mglru+ghost-admission: refaulting folios added to youngest gen. Prior eval failed verifier: ghost tier index unbounded in update_refaulted_stat -> masked with & (MAX_NR_TIERS-1).

structural 3/3 history-LFU: v2 (551) + 1s grace for newly inserted folios (score 2^40+count). Hypothesis: throughput tracks bytes/disk-IO (readahead health: ref 12.4KB->497, LFU 13->544, s3fifo 15.5->642, mglru 16.8->645); LFU evicted fresh count-0 readahead pages

history-LFU via ITERATE not SAMPLE: same persistent freq sketch + 1s grace as 541-551 versions, but eviction = CLOCK threshold passes (count<=1,<=3,<=8,any) with list_iterate. Tests whether list_sample itself is the bottleneck (all 5 sample-based team attempts 497-551, all iterate-based >=600)
reviewer: same-host pair. reference/mglru.c unchanged on pc309, where noop = 640.4 (ad992e58). Other hosts: mglru 645 (pc319), 652 (nemo). Tests whether MGLRU really beats kernel default

mglru-tune 2/3: tune1 (tail insert) LOST 565->538, so evicting newest-inserted never-accessed folios (accesses==1, i.e. unconsumed/unused readahead) first is GOOD. Push it: always insert new folios into OLDEST gen head (ref uses min_seq+1 when >3 gens). Base = mglru ref (head insert)

reviewer: unmodified noop.c on pc306 to anchor my host. ahab: noop=640 on pc309, jack: 561 on pc320 -> hosts differ ~14%. My pc306: mglru 652, s3fifo 642/635/633/637. If noop ~640-650 here, no team policy yet beats kernel default meaningfully.

structural 1/3 region-frequency CLOCK: f2ca3e81 (617, history-LFU via iterate) with the persistent counter keyed by (ino, index>>4) = 64KB regions, so readahead batches are kept/evicted as a unit (hypothesis: FIFO/MGLRU win via batch-coherent eviction -> larger refault IOs on a ~280 IOPS disk)

mglru lane 2/3: reference mglru (652; noop on pc306 = 628) with new folios added at TAIL of gen list instead of head. Ref list_add puts new folios at the eviction end of oldest/2nd-oldest gen -> near-immediate eviction unless re-referenced. Tests whether that aggressive new-page filtering is mglru's edge. (1/3 ghost->youngest gen = 634, worse.)
mglru-tune 3/3: tune2 (always-oldest-gen insert, 574.5, my best vs ref 565) + refaulted folios whose ghost tier>=1 (accessed before eviction) inserted into youngest gen (max_seq) instead of oldest
mglru + access aging: halve folio access count (min 1) on each tier-protection promotion, like kernel folio_inc_gen clearing refs. Ref mglru never decays. Same-host base: mglru 668.8, noop 640.4
structural 2/3 region-frequency CLOCK: REGION_SHIFT 4->5 (128KB regions = default readahead window). Parent f578a1ba = 672

reviewer replication: davy-jones f578a1ba region-frequency CLOCK (672 on pc319) UNCHANGED on pc306. My pc306 anchors: noop 628, mglru 652, s3fifo ~637. Also: mglru with tail insertion = 608 (-7%) -> mglru's edge is head insertion (new pages evicted first unless re-referenced).
structural 3/3 region-frequency CLOCK: REGION_SHIFT 3 (32KB). Sweep so far: shift4(64KB)=672 f578a1ba, shift5(128KB)=651 38ee907f, page-level(shift0)=617 f2ca3e81
cross-host replication: davy-jones f578a1ba region-frequency CLOCK (672 on pc319) unchanged (comment only) on pc320. pc320 refs: mglru 565, mglru-tune2 574.5, noop 561

structural 1/3 MGLRU + persistent region tiers: tier = f(folio accesses + decayed 64KB-region access count/4), region counters in 1M-slot array map (survive eviction, halve per ~8.6s idle). On top of 0a062399 (674). Composes davy-jones region-freq (f578a1ba) with MGLRU

region-CLOCK grace sweep 1/2: davy-jones f578a1ba (683 on pc306) with GRACE_NS 1s -> 200ms. Motivation: mglru head- vs tail-insertion (652 vs 608) says evicting un-re-referenced new pages early helps; 1s grace may over-protect readahead/one-shot regions.
region-frequency CLOCK sweep: REGION_SHIFT 2 (16KB). So far shift0 617, shift3 682, shift4 672, shift5 651 (pc319)

region-freq CLOCK (davy f578a1ba; replicated 582.7 on pc320 = +3.1% over mglru 565) + grace only when region count>0: never-accessed (prefetch-only) regions are immediate victims, combining my mglru-tune2 finding (evict never-accessed early: 565->574.5)

structural 1/3 (verifier fix: hash i_ino not host ptr) MGLRU + persistent region tiers: tier from folio accesses + decayed 64KB-region count/4 (1M-slot array, halve per ~8.6s idle). Base 0a062399 (674)
region-CLOCK combo: GRACE_NS 200ms (mine, 690 on pc306 vs 683 at 1s) + REGION_SHIFT 3 (davy-jones best on pc319: 682 vs 672 at shift 4).
region-freq CLOCK shift3 (682) + CLOCK pass thresholds 1/3/8 -> 2/6/16 (region counters aggregate 8 pages so counts run higher)

region-freq CLOCK knob nobody is sweeping: AGE_SHIFT 18->15 (8x faster count halving; at 2^18 counts barely decay within a 30s run). Base davy f578a1ba = 582.7 on pc320. Grace-only-if-accessed tweak reverted (568.5, lost)

region-CLOCK grace sweep 2/2: GRACE_NS 50ms, REGION_SHIFT 4. pc306 so far: grace 1s=683, 200ms=690, 200ms+shift3=687 (all within noise). Tests whether shorter grace keeps helping (mglru head-insert lesson) or if grace barely matters.

cross-host replication of team-best config: captain-nemo 51067b5b (region-freq CLOCK, REGION_SHIFT 3, GRACE 200ms; 687 on pc306) unchanged on pc320. pc320 base: f578a1ba (shift4, grace 1s) = 582.7/584.3, mglru 565
region-freq CLOCK: nemo combo 51067b5b (shift3 + grace 200ms, 687 pc306) + DEDUPE 2ms->20ms (region count = number of distinct 20ms windows with an access; less burst-inflated). Untouched knob

region-CLOCK DEDUPE_NS 2ms -> 20ms (untaken knob) on my best 3f1573c8 (shift4, grace 200ms, 690). Region counter aggregates 16 pages; a scan burst through one 64KB region may span >2ms and inflate the count. Grace sweep on pc306 was flat: 1s 683 / 200ms 690 / 50ms 688.
region-freq CLOCK 50b9f179 (690) with LOWER CLOCK thresholds 1/3/8 -> 0/1/3 (raising to 2/6/16 lost 682->658, so test the other direction)

region-freq CLOCK pass thresholds (1,3,8) -> (2,4,16) on team-best nemo 51067b5b (593.6 on pc320). Untouched knob: first pass now also evicts regions read twice (more FIFO-like for lukewarm regions, LevelDB block cache flattens page-level freq)

variance repeat (final eval 20/20): 3f1573c8 unchanged except comment (region-CLOCK shift4, grace 200ms; first run 690.0). pc306 region-CLOCK family so far 683-690 for grace/shift/dedupe variants; this measures same-code spread.
thresholds trend test: (2,4,16)=607.1 > (1,3,8)=593.6 on pc320; now (3,6,24) on nemo 51067b5b base
final: resubmit of 50b9f179 (region-freq CLOCK, 690.3) with a comment-only change, to measure same-host run-to-run variance

Hypothesis: GET miss = random seek, scan miss amortised by readahead, so GET-read regions worth more. Caveat: if scan_pids is empty, acts like halved thresholds
confirmation re-run of 6b62bff1 thresholds (2,4,16) (607.1). Neighbors on pc320: (1,3,8)=593.6, (3,6,24)=585.3

same-host control: team-best 50b9f179 (region-CLOCK) unchanged (comment only) on pc309, to attribute my c56fed27 GET x2 result (699.6, same host). jack pc320: weighting 583 vs base 594

repeat of 0a187508 (region-CLOCK + region-coherent eviction, 711.2) unchanged except comment, to confirm +2.2% over same-host control 695.6
region-coherent eviction DOOM_NS 100ms -> 300ms (base 7e6df4dc confirmed 711.2/712.2 on pc309). Longer doom window catches region-mates further down the CLOCK list
